cues.en: Now calling fetch here is an option and works just fine for us here.
Still, I would recommend that you actually don't do it here directly in the script tags, but instead
that you use on mount.
In some situations, like for example, when you're adding server side rendering, which we haven't
yet but which we'll learn about later, this can be preferable and in other situations it simply the
same and you have no real disadvantage.
So therefore I would recommend using on mount here pass in a function and in that function you then
execute this fetch call.
This will still run when this component is mounted.
But again, in some situations this is better.
In other situations it simply won't make a difference.
So with that it still works as before.
But again on mount would be my recommendation if you need to fetch data on the initial load.
Please also be aware that you have to define hobbies here before you fetch.
So what won't work is that you define hobbies in here for multiple reasons.
For one, this would scope the variable to this inner function and would not expose it to the entire
component.
And even if it would, it would define it too late because this runs, even if you put it outside of
on mount to late fetch here sends a request.
And of course JavaScript doesn't wait for this request to finish before it continues parsing the rest
of the script so it would finish parsing everything and rendering the component before you got the response.
Now in the component you are relying on hobbies and therefore if you only define hobbies in there,
which happens in the future and not immediately, you would first render the component without a hobbies
variable, not just without a value but without a variable.
And that of course would lead to errors.
And therefore you have to define all the variables.
You're using your markup first and then if you are loading data for that asynchronously so the data
arrives in the future, you can overwrite the values as I'm doing it here, but you have to define it
here first.
Now, of course, you might want to show some loading spinner whilst you are loading for the data.
And therefore of course here we can also set is loading to true and then change it back to false once
we got our data.
So set loading to false here and also in the case of an error, if you are doing that, then of course
you again will show that loading spinner before you show anything else.
So if this reloads, you briefly see that loading spinner and you have to watch really close because
Firebase is so fast.
But here is the loading spinner or the loading text in this case.
